akhfash:15-16.t: He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ﴾ ﴿نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ﴾: accusative as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ (the pronoun)**, and the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" is ﴿نزَاعةٌ﴾. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the text appears disturbed here, since it explains the accusative نَزَّاعَةً and then names the nominative نَزَّاعَةٌ as the predicate.]» And if you wish, you make ﴿لَظَى﴾ nominative as the khabar of ﴿إِنَّ﴾ and make "النزّاعة" nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾, then He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ﴾: He made ﴿الإِنْسانَ﴾ a plurality, and what shows you this is that He has excepted a plurality from it.

akhfash:36-37.t: And He said ﴿فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ﴾, just as you say "ما لَكَ قَائِماً" ("why are you standing?"). The singular of "العِزِينَ" is العِزَةُ (a band), like "ثُبَة" and "ثُبِين".
